DaVinci, pack what's ours and leave what isn't. Michelangelo, when you're ready — no rush, you've got time — help me sort what stays from what goes.

Donatello, whatever's in that notebook is worth keeping intact. Make sure it's secure before we board anything.

Three hours is enough time to do this right. Let's do it right.

records.response_pred:
Michelangelo, that's a good point about the disappearing thing. I think it's something that'll be difficult to quantify, but if we're being honest, it's probably going to be one of the hardest things to do when you're the one who's not there to witness it.

I'd also try to be more decisive and follow the plan more closely. When we're all in the same boat, it's easy to get caught up in the fray and second-guess ourselves, but when you're the one who's responsible for making a decision, you can be more confident in your choices. I'd try to trust my instincts more and follow the plan more closely.

Lastly, I'd try to be more empathetic and supportive of my fellow crew members. When things are going badly, it's easy to get caught up in your own problems and forget about those around you, but when you're in a crisis, you need to be there for those who are struggling. I'd try to be more supportive and nurturing, especially to those who are feeling the most overwhelmed or anxious.
